sources.title: John Tsitsiklis, MIT 6.041SC Lecture 1 Probability Models and Axioms
sources.checked: Opened official resource and actual 4-page PDF; read pages1-3: sample space completeness/exclusivity, events as subsets, nonnegative normalized probabilities, finite and countable additivity, counting only under equal likelihood. Course uses finite spaces throughout and does not claim a general measure-theory construction.

sources.title: John Tsitsiklis, MIT 6.041SC Lecture 2 Conditioning and Bayes' Rule
sources.checked: Read actual PDF pages1-2: conditional sample space, positive conditioning denominator, multiplication chain, partition-weighted total probability and Bayes normalization. Text extraction damaged one not-equal symbol; positive-denominator condition is independently explicit in Lecture3 page1 and in the definition. Original device table and calculations were developed independently.

sources.title: John Tsitsiklis, MIT 6.041SC Lecture 3 Independence
sources.checked: Read actual PDF pages1-2: symmetric event-independence product definition, zero-probability cases, independence under a conditional law, conditioning can change independence, and pairwise versus joint independence. Course's exact synthetic regime tables and all original figure implementations were checked with integer/Fraction arithmetic.

sources.title: NumPy 2.3 Generator.multinomial official reference
sources.checked: Read official parameters and returns: n nonnegative trial count, p-dimensional category probabilities, size + (p,) output, last category residual implementation detail. Actual runtime NumPy2.3.5 output shape (400,4), nonnegative integer counts and row sums n tested. The course validates the entire probability vector and does not rely on silently filling an invalid last entry.

sources.title: Pearl, Glymour and Jewell, Causal Inference in Statistics A Primer, author-hosted chapter3 preview
sources.checked: Read Section3.1, printed pages54-55 (PDF pages2-3): conditioning filters naturally observed cases; intervention modifies a mechanism; observational and intervention distributions need not coincide. Course includes only an original device-light explanation and does not teach identification or estimate an intervention effect. The preview itself is not redistributed.

mathematical_conditions_checked: Finite weighted sample space versus equal-probability counting
Conditional denominator strictly positive; finite observed zero is not model probability zero
Total probability requires a disjoint exhaustive partition and target-population weights
Bayes normalization requires positive evidence mass; likelihood vector need not sum to one
Repeated likelihood multiplication needs conditional independence within each hypothesis
Event independence distinct from mutual exclusivity; degenerate events allowed by product definition
Conditional independence and unconditional independence imply neither another in general
Pairwise independence does not guarantee joint independence
Zero covariance is weaker than independence except for the special pair of binary indicators
Finite repeated-experiment percentile range is not a parameter confidence interval
retrieval_limits: Read the listed relevant lecture sections, not the full textbooks or videos.
An older author-hosted chapter extract had garbled text and was not used; the readable Primer chapter3 preview was used instead.
independent_authorship: Original Chinese exposition, device example, finite counts, figures, lab, solutions and code. Sources verify definitions and assumptions; source PDFs, figures and copyrighted prose are not copied into the payload. No license is asserted for third-party sources.
